{{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox NCAA team season |mode=Basketball |year=2016–17 |team=Dayton Flyers |image=Dayton Flyers logo.svg |image_size=150 |conference=Atlantic 10 Conference |division= |short_conf=A-10 |CoachRank= |APRank= |record= 24–8 |conf_record=15–3 |head_coach=[[Archie Miller (basketball)|Archie Miller]] |hc_year = 6th |asst_coach1=[[Kevin Kuwik]] |asst_coach2=Allen Griffin |asst_coach3=Tom Ostrom |asst_coach4= |stadium=[[University of Dayton Arena]] |champion= Atlantic 10 regular season champions |bowl=[[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |bowl_result = First Round }} {{2016–17 Atlantic 10 men's basketball standings}} The '''2016–17 Dayton Flyers men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Dayton]] during the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Flyers, led by sixth-year head coach [[Archie Miller (basketball)|Archie Miller]], played their home games at the [[University of Dayton Arena]] as members of the [[Atlantic 10 Conference]]. They finished the season 24–8, 15–3 in [[2016–17 Atlantic 10 Conference men's basketball season|A-10 play]] to win the regular season A-10 championship. They received the No. 1 seed in the [[2017 Atlantic 10 men's basketball tournament|A-10 tournament]] where they lost in the quarterfinals to [[2016–17 Davidson Wildcats men's basketball team|Davidson]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they lost in the first round to [[2016-17 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|Wichita State]]. On March 25, 2017, Archie Miller left the school to accept the head coaching position at [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]].{{cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/19001709/archie-miller-coach-indiana-hoosiers |title=Hoosiers hire Dayton's Archie Miller as coach |first1=Jeff |last1=Goodman |first2=Andy |last2=Katz |authorlink2=Andy Katz |publisher=ESPN.com |date=March 25, 2017 |accessdate=March 25, 2017}}{{Cite news|url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/indiana/2017/03/25/report-archie-miller-new-iu-coach/99618342/|title=Archie Miller 'a great hire for IU, great hire for the state'|work=Indianapolis Star|access-date=2017-03-27|language=en}} He finished at Dayton with a six year record of 139–63. The school then hired Dayton alum [[Anthony Grant (basketball)|Anthony Grant]] as the new head coach on March 30.{{cite press release|url=http://www.daytonflyers.com/news/2017/3/30/anthony-grant-named-new-dayton-mens-basketball-coach.aspx|title=Anthony Grant Named New Dayton Men's Basketball Coach|publisher=[[Dayton Flyers]]|date=March 30, 2017|accessdate=July 18, 2017}} ==Previous season== The [[2015–16 Dayton Flyers men's basketball team|Flyers]] finished the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2015–16 season]] with a record of 25–8, 14–4 in A-10 play to become regular season [[2015–16 Atlantic 10 Conference men's basketball season|A-10 co-champions]]. They defeated [[2015–16 Richmond Spiders men's basketball team|Richmond]] in the quarterfinals of the [[2016 Atlantic 10 men's basketball tournament|A-10 tournament]] to advance to the semifinals where they lost to [[2015–16 Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball team|Saint Joseph's]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2006 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], their third consecutive at-large bid, as a No. 7 seed in the Midwest Region where they lost to No. 10 seed [[2015-16 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]] in the first round. == Preseason == The Flyers were picked to win the A-10 in the conference's preseason poll.{{Cite press release|url=http://www.atlantic10.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=31600&ATCLID=211235312|title=Flyers Picked to Win 2016-17 Men's Basketball |publisher=Atlantic 10 Conference |accessdate=November 7, 2016}} Charles Cooke and Scoochie Smith were selected to the preseason All-A-10 first team.
